report.summary: Outbox publications lagged arrivals for about 2 minutes, with the oldest undelivered event reaching 25 s before the backlog drained. A consumer handler delay of about 310 ms on some attempts is the likely cause. No failures or DB/pool contention were seen.

findings.claim: A delivery backlog formed mid-window and then drained: pending rose to 77 and the oldest undelivered event aged to 25.5 s.
findings.reason: Publications ran at 19-24 per 10 s against about 30 arrivals, then burst to 79 and 55 per 10 s. Pending fell back to 2 by the end.

findings.claim: The consumer handler was slow on some attempts: handler p95 is 310 ms against a p50 of 0.023 ms, which pushes total p95 to 387 ms.
findings.reason: Auth (about 70 ms) and unattributed time are small and stable, so the tail comes from consumer handler time.

findings.claim: There were no delivery failures or retries, so the lateness comes from reduced delivery throughput, not from errors.
findings.reason: All 541 attempts succeeded on attempt 1 with status 200, and the failed count stayed at 0.

findings.claim: The transfer API, DB pool and DB locking look healthy and are unlikely causes.
findings.reason: Transfer p99 was 0.25 s with no 5xx, the pool had no pending borrowers or timeouts, and no DB blocking was sampled.

limitations: Handler delay is measured by a test-fixture consumer, so it may not match the real notification consumer.
The delivery log listing covers only the first 100 of 541 records, and none from the backlog period (about 15:17:57 onward) are shown.

report.summary: Outbox publications fell below arrivals for about 70 s, so pending and oldest-undelivered age grew to about 25 s before draining. The consumer handler was intermittently slow (about 310 ms); the cause of the dip is not confirmed.

findings.claim: Outbox backlog built then drained: publications ran about 19-24 per 10s vs about 30 arrivals; pending peaked at 77 and oldest age at 25.5s.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts and gauges show the shortfall, then catch-up bursts of 79 and 55, matching late notifications.

findings.claim: Delivery itself never failed: all 541 attempts succeeded on attempt 1, with zero failures, auth errors or server errors.
findings.reason: Delivery logs show only SUCCESS and the failed gauge stayed at 0, so retries or backoff don't explain the delay.

findings.claim: A slow consumer handler (p95 310ms vs p50 0.023ms) probably slowed poll batches and cut publish throughput, creating the backlog.
findings.reason: Slow handler calls appear in the timings, and the poller uses one-second polls with batches of 20. No per-time breakdown ties them to the dip.

limitations: The handler slowness is not time-aligned with the 15:18-15:19 dip, and the consumer is a test fixture.
Only the earliest 100 delivery log rows are listed, so the dip window's individual attempts weren't inspected.
